title: Traffic fencing and model admission controller for heterogeneous environments
creator: Priya Shah
description:
Problem: We lack a single, lightweight mechanism to safely admit and fence model traffic across Hosted, Dedicated and Private installs. Existing rollout tooling assumes uniform networking and capacity semantics; Private/VPC and Dedicated clusters impose per-tenant quotas, stricter egress rules, and slower kernel upgrade windows. That mismatch has caused noisy canaries and manual intervention during several recent model promotions.

Goal: Build a model admission controller + traffic fencing primitives that: 1) enforces per-environment constraints (capacity, network policy, KMS availability), 2) performs fast local rejection for incompatible requests, 3) integrates with canary/A-B/shadow flows to prevent noisy experiments from spilling into production, and 4) emits clear signals for automated rollback and human ops. The controller must be lightweight (config-first), pluggable into Redwood routing layer, and backward compatible with existing rollout APIs.
acceptance_criteria: Admission controller evaluates a model promotion request and returns allow/deny with a human-readable reason within 30ms for Hosted and Dedicated control planes.
Traffic fencing can tag and isolate experimental traffic (by customer, route, or header) and enforce per-tenant concurrent request caps at the routing edge.

Auto-rollback hooks consume the controllers signals and can trigger rollback when configured composite SLO breaches occur (example: 5xx rate > 0.5% AND p95 latency increase > 20% over baseline for 3 minutes).
Private deployments can opt out of automatic rollback and receive audit events to their on-prem audit sink instead.
Comprehensive e2e tests and a sandbox demo route are available in the console for PM/SEs to run A/B and shadow tests without modifying service code.
tasks: Design admission controller config schema and pact with routing layer (config fields: env_constraints, capacity_hard_limits, allowed_kms_profiles, network_whitelist)
Implement lightweight admission evaluator in routing plane (Go) with caching of environment metadata
Add traffic fencing tags to the router and propagate to runtime for per-model concurrency accounting
Wire admission events to observability: new metrics (admissions_allowed, admissions_denied_by_reason, fencing_hits) and audit log entries
Define rollback signal composition and implement a first-pass auto-rollback plugin that listens to metric streams
Create Confluence runbook and demo workspace for QE/SEs, plus e2e test harness for Hosted/Dedicated/Private variants
signal_definitions: 5xx_rate: percentage of server errors for a route over a 1m window; rollback threshold: >0.5% sustained for 3m
p95_latency_rel: p95 latency relative increase vs baseline; rollback threshold: >20% sustained for 3m
error_budget_burn: sudden spike in token-level cost or retries; advisory threshold: 3x normal burn rate in 5m
progress_updates: 2026-02-25: Spike complete. Evaluated two approaches: (A) admission as a pre-routing plugin, (B) admission as part of the control-plane policy engine. Chosen pre-routing plugin for lower blast radius and sub-30ms latency.
2026-03-03: Prototype merged for Hosted; includes basic env metadata cache and deny reasons. Running internal smoke tests against canary workflows.

2026-03-08: Design review with PM/Design. PM requested a clearer surface for opt-out in Private installs and a tenant-visible denial reason. Added spec item to propagate user-friendly reasons to console.

2026-03-12: Began work on Dedicated capacity cap enforcement; discovered race in concurrency counters when traffic is split across nodes. Added task to add sharded counters with periodic reconciliation.

qa_plan: Unit tests for admission evaluator with mocked env metadata
Integration tests that run Hosted vs Dedicated mode in CI with simulated capacity constraints
Manual validation in sandbox org: create A/B experiment with <1% traffic, confirm fencing tags and admission events
Private QA: deliver a Helm values patch that exercises opt-out and confirms audit sink delivery
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: False positives in admission deny could block legitimate traffic. Mitigation: default to permissive mode + dry-run for first ramp, escalation path in console.
Risk: Increased latency at routing edge. Mitigation: keep evaluator stateless and cached; fall back to control-plane check only on cache misses.
Risk: Feature divergence across Private installs due to slower upgrade cadence. Mitigation: explicit opt-out and audit-only modes for Private, plus backward-compatible config fields.
notes: Do not break existing rollout APIs. The admission controller should evaluate but not mutate routing decisions unless a deny is returned.
Coordinate with Console team for UX that surfaces denial reasons and offers one-click override where policy allows.
Follow-up epic will expose a policy DSL for more complex A/B guardrails if this MVP proves effective.
